title: statim • Higher Level Interface for Statistical Inference
text: R rich statistical ecosystem, hypothesis testing served assortment disconnected functions. R gained grammar graphics (ggplot2) one data manipulation (dplyr), statistical inference equivalent: testing function ships interface, way specifying data, output format. shared grammar inference: way say want test without simultaneously committing procedure carries . statim attempt re-imagine ground , way ggplot2 introduced grammar graphics without replacing base plotting functions. core idea inferential procedure can described three steps: define structure data (define_model()), declare want infer (prepare_test()), optionally recalibrate estimation method (via()). procedure executes call conclude(). separation matters makes statistical workflows composable. Switching classical permutation procedure require rewriting code; single addition pipeline:
code: # Classical t-test sleep |> define_model(x_by(extra, group)) |> prepare_test(TTEST) |> conclude()  # Permutation t-test: one line added, nothing else changes sleep |> define_model(x_by(extra, group)) |> prepare_test(TTEST) |> via("permute", n = 1000L) |> conclude()  # The same pipeline shape works for any registered test cars |> define_model(rel(speed, dist)) |> prepare_test(CORTEST) |> conclude()  # For a quick result, the eager form skips the pipeline entirely TTEST(x_by(extra, group), sleep) CORTEST(rel(speed, dist), cars)

title: statim • Higher Level Interface for Statistical Inference
text: package designed around three ideas: shared grammar: every inferential procedure follows shape – define_model(), prepare_test(), conclude() – regardless test model ID used. model ID objects (e.g. x_by, rel, pairwise) determines test ; grammar stays . Eager forms (TTEST(), CORTEST(), …) provide shortcut full pipeline needed. Composable pipelines: build test specification lazily, recalibrate estimation method single via() call, execute conclude(). Extensible design: every test stat_define() object; bring engine, method, implementation. Auto dispatch handles tidy() method without requiring write .

what: Structured result container for GLM fits — class_glm_object
title: Structured result container for GLM fits — class_glm_object
text: S7 class produced GLM pipelines. constructed manually — use define_model() |> prepare_model(GLM) |> conclude() instead. Inherits anova_able, participates anova() directly. Downstream packages can use parent S7::new_class().

title: Structured result container for GLM fits — class_glm_object
text: Constructor arguments (populated automatically GLM): terms: model terms object. df_residual: residual degrees freedom. deviance: scalar deviance. dispersion: scalar dispersion parameter. family: string naming error family, e.g. "binomial". coefficients: data frame columns term, estimate, std_error, statistic, p_value. fit_summary: data frame columns family, link, null_deviance, deviance, df_residual, aic, n_obs.

title: Structured result container for GLM fits — class_glm_object
code: # Inheriting from class_glm_object in a downstream package: my_glm = S7::new_class(     "my_glm",     parent = class_glm_object )  # Populating class_glm_object from a fitted glm (as done internally): fit = glm(am ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars, family = binomial()) s = summary(fit) fam = fit$family$family  obj = class_glm_object(     terms = fit$terms,     df_residual = fit$df.residual,     deviance = fit$deviance,     dispersion = if (fam %in% c("binomial", "poisson")) 1 else s$dispersion,     family = fam,     coefficients = tibble::tibble(         term = rownames(coef(s)),         estimate = coef(s)[, 1],         std_error = coef(s)[, 2],         statistic = coef(s)[, 3],         p_value = coef(s)[, 4]     ),     fit_summary = tibble::tibble(         family = fam,         link = fit$family$link,         null_deviance = fit$null.deviance,         deviance = fit$deviance,         df_residual = as.integer(fit$df.residual),         aic = fit$aic,         n_obs = as.integer(length(fit$residuals))     ) )

what: Structured result container for linear model fits — class_lm_object
title: Structured result container for linear model fits — class_lm_object
text: S7 class produced LINEAR_REG pipelines. constructed manually — use define_model() |> prepare_model(LINEAR_REG) |> conclude() instead. Inherits anova_able, participates anova() directly. Downstream packages can use parent S7::new_class().

title: Structured result container for linear model fits — class_lm_object
text: Constructor arguments (populated automatically LINEAR_REG): terms: model terms object. df_residual: residual degrees freedom. deviance: residual sum squares (RSS). dispersion: mean squared error (MSE), .e. rss / df_residual. family: always "gaussian" OLS. fitted: numeric vector fitted values. residuals: numeric vector model residuals. beta: named numeric vector coefficient estimates. std_beta: named numeric vector coefficient standard errors. x_mat: model matrix stored flat numeric vector via .numeric(stats::model.matrix(fit)). Required single-model anova(); omit Type ANOVA needed. following computed automatically need supplied: statistic: per-coefficient t-statistics (beta / std_beta). p_value: per-coefficient two-sided p-values. coefficients: tibble columns term, estimate, std_error, statistic, p_value. fit_summary: two-column tibble (statistic, value) R-squared, adjusted R-squared, sigma, n, residual df, F-statistic, df1, df2, F p-value.

title: Structured result container for linear model fits — class_lm_object
text: class_lm_object supports two anova() modes: Single model — Type (sequential) ANOVA. term tested model containing preceding terms. Requires x_mat populated. Multiple models — incremental F-test LRT across nested models. Uses @deviance @df_residual ; x_mat needed.

title: Structured result container for linear model fits — class_lm_object
code: # Inheriting from class_lm_object in a downstream package: my_lm = S7::new_class(     "my_lm",     parent = statim::class_lm_object )  # Populating class_lm_object from a fitted lm (as done internally): fit = lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars) coef_tbl = summary(fit)$coefficients rss = sum(fit$residuals^2) df_res = fit$df.residual  obj = class_lm_object(     terms = fit$terms,     fitted = unname(fit$fitted.values),     residuals = unname(fit$residuals),     beta = coef_tbl[, 1],     std_beta = coef_tbl[, 2],     df_residual = df_res,     deviance = rss,     dispersion = rss / df_res,     family = "gaussian",     x_mat = as.numeric(stats::model.matrix(fit)) )  obj@coefficients #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   term        estimate std_error statistic  p_value #>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)   -17.6      6.76      -2.60 1.23e- 2 #> 2 speed           3.93     0.416      9.46 1.49e-12 obj@fit_summary #> # A tibble: 9 × 2 #>   statistic         value #>   <chr>             <dbl> #> 1 R Squared      6.51e- 1 #> 2 Adj. R Squared 6.44e- 1 #> 3 Sigma          1.54e+ 1 #> 4 n              5   e+ 1 #> 5 df (residual)  4.8 e+ 1 #> 6 F-statistic    8.96e+ 1 #> 7 df1            1   e+ 0 #> 8 df2            4.8 e+ 1 #> 9 p-value        1.49e-12
